instruction: Open Chrome and navigate to Google Scholar.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly reads the Chrome address bar URL from the accessibility tree, specifically targeting 'application[name=Google Chrome] entry[name=Address and search bar]', which directly verifies that Chrome is open and focused on the expected URL.

Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly handles the expected parameter: when expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly, and the function accesses rules['expected'] = ['scholar\\.google\\.com'] correctly.
The regex pattern 'scholar\\.google\\.com' correctly matches any URL on Google Scholar (e.g., https://scholar.google.com/), covering the full instruction requirement.

Negative-control resistance is sound: the initial state has a PDF viewer open (not Chrome on Scholar), so the getter returns None or cannot find Chrome's address bar, causing the metric to return 0.0 — correctly failing the initial state.

Full instruction coverage: the evaluator checks both that Chrome is open (getter targets Chrome's accessibility tree node) and that it is navigated to Google Scholar (regex URL match), satisfying both sub-goals of the instruction.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent read shi17a.pdf, identified corresponding author Tianlin (Tim) Shi (Stanford), but failed to open Chrome and navigate to Google Scholar after 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Agent can read PDF documents, identify corresponding author info, and open Chrome browser. Demonstrated Chrome navigation to google.com in later steps.
metadata.failure_analysis: Agent failed around step 7 when trying to open a new Chrome tab from within the PDF viewer. It confused the PDF viewer with Chrome, eventually opening Chrome separately but running out of turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplifies the original task to just opening Chrome and going to scholar.google.com — removing the harder sub-goal of finding a specific author profile. This is achievable within the reliable prefix actions (opening Chrome).
metadata.explanation: Task requires the agent to open Chrome and navigate to Google Scholar (scholar.google.com). Evaluator checks the active URL in the accessibility tree using regex pattern match. Initial state (PDF viewer open, Chrome not open) fails the evaluator. Only succeeds when Chrome shows scholar.google.com.
